"'''Cradle of Love'''" is a song by the English [[Rock music|rock]] singer [[Billy Idol]], released in 1990 as the first single from his fourth studio album, ''[[Charmed Life (Billy Idol album)|Charmed Life]]''. The song was written by [[David Werner (musician)|David Werner]] and Idol, and was produced by [[Keith Forsey]]. It became Idol's last top-10 hit in the United States, where it reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 2 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. It was also Idol's first and only No. 1 hit on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Mainstream Rock Tracks|Album Rock Tracks]] chart. On the [[UK Single Chart]], it stalled at No. 34.

"Cradle of Love" is a song by the English rock singer Billy Idol, released in 1990 as the first single from his fourth studio album, Charmed Life. The song was written by David Werner and Idol, and was produced by Keith Forsey. It became Idol's last top-10 hit in the United States, where it reached {{abbr|No.|Number}} 2 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was also Idol's first and only No. 1 hit on the Billboard Album Rock Tracks chart. On the UK Single Chart, it stalled at No. 34.

sections.heading: Music and lyrics
sections.wikitext:
"Cradle of Love" is a [[New wave music|new wave]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carlson |first=Taylor |title=Billy Idol – The Vegas Residency has Begun! |url=https://zrockr.com/2016/04/06/billy-idol-residency/ |access-date=April 25, 2025 |website=ZRockR |date=April 6, 2016}}</ref> and [[hard rock]] song<ref>{{cite book|first=Vladimir|last=Bogdanov|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/All_Music_Guide_to_Rock/1-pH4i3jXvAC?hl=en&gbpv=1|title=All Music Guide to Rock: The Definitive Guide to Rock, Pop, and Soul|date=November 27, 2002|access-date=March 14, 2025|publisher=[[Backbeat Books]]|page=556}}</ref> with a [[doo-wop]] melody,<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Encyclopedia_of_Punk_Rock_and_New_Wave/6I88EQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1|title=Encyclopedia of Punk Rock and New Wave: 1975–1985|date=January 9, 2025|access-date=March 14, 2025|publisher=[[Bloomsbury Publishing]]|first1=David|first2=Michael|last1=Luhrssen|last2=Larson|page=1972}}</ref> influenced by '50s [[Rock and roll|rock 'n' roll]] and "[[Ramones]]-esque [[Punk rock|punk]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peacock |first=Tim |date=2024-11-30 |title=The Best Billy Idol Songs: A Master Of Reinvention |url=https://www.udiscovermusic.com/stories/best-billy-idol-songs-feature/ |access-date=2025-04-25 |website=uDiscover Music |language=en-US}}</ref> It is composed in [[common time]] and in the key of [[B flat major|B{{music|flat}} major]].<ref name="sheet">Sheet music for "Cradle of Love". [[Hal Leonard Publishing]]. 1990.</ref> The song title is supposedly based on the saying "[[Age disparity in sexual relationships|robbing the cradle]]".

"Cradle of Love" was originally written solely by [[David Werner (musician)|David Werner]]. In 1989, he demoed the song and a number of other tracks with Mark Doyle on guitar, Tom Bellin on bass and Rob Deaner on keyboards. Werner then shopped the demos to various record labels in the attempt to gain their interest. He was left to choose between signing his own album recording deal with CBS Records or giving "Cradle of Love" to Billy Idol to record through Elektra Records for an upcoming film, ''[[The Adventures of Ford Fairlane]]''. He decided on the latter option after Idol's label Chrysalis also expressed interest in including the track on the singer's next album, ''Charmed Life''. Idol received a co-writing credit after he made some changes and additions to the lyrics during its recording.<ref>{{cite news |last=King |first=Peter B. |title=Whiz kid rocks the 'Cradle' for Idol |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/146452558/ |newspaper=[[The Pittsburgh Press]] |date=9 September 1990 |page=F4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 April 2025}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Cradle of Love" is a new wave and hard rock song with a doo-wop melody, influenced by '50s rock 'n' roll and "Ramones-esque punk". It is composed in common time and in the key of B{{music|flat}} major. The song title is supposedly based on the saying "robbing the cradle".

"Cradle of Love" was originally written solely by David Werner. In 1989, he demoed the song and a number of other tracks with Mark Doyle on guitar, Tom Bellin on bass and Rob Deaner on keyboards. Werner then shopped the demos to various record labels in the attempt to gain their interest. He was left to choose between signing his own album recording deal with CBS Records or giving "Cradle of Love" to Billy Idol to record through Elektra Records for an upcoming film, The Adventures of Ford Fairlane. He decided on the latter option after Idol's label Chrysalis also expressed interest in including the track on the singer's next album, Charmed Life. Idol received a co-writing credit after he made some changes and additions to the lyrics during its recording.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Upon its release as a single, Gary Crossing of ''[[Record Mirror]]'' commented that Idol "sneers, growls and rebel yells his way through another laughable, leatherclad anthem".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Crossing |first=Gary |title=Singles |magazine=[[Record Mirror]] |date=21 April 1990 |page=16 |issn=0144-5804}}</ref> Phil Wilding of ''[[Kerrang!]]'' concluded, "Getting hit off his bike has obviously caused Billy to slip into regression and convince himself that he's [[Marc Bolan]]. He's dead, Billy. Wake up and smell the earth."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Wilding |first=Phil |title=Singlez |magazine=[[Kerrang!]] |date=28 April 1990 |issue=287 |page=11 |issn=0262-6624}}</ref> In the US, ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' remarked that "Idol fans will relish in the singer's familiar, quick-paced, guitar-driven pop".<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Single Reviews |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=28 April 1990 |publisher=Billboard Publications, Inc. |volume=102 |issue=17 |page=73 |issn=0006-2510}}</ref>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
{{Refimprove section|date=November 2021}}
[[File:Billy-idol-cradle-of-love-tour.jpg|thumb|A photo of Billy Idol taken during the Cradle of Love Tour. The jacket is the same jacket that he wears in the video.]]
The video, directed by [[David Fincher]], features footage of Idol singing in large painting frames throughout an apartment. The director made the decision to film Idol from the waist up as he was unable to walk due to injuries from a February 1990 motorcycle crash.<ref>Prato, Greg [{{Allmusic|class=artist|id=p4540|pure_url=yes}} "Biography of Billy Idol"]. ''[[Allmusic]]''. Retrieved 4 November 2007.</ref> The video also features Betsy Lynn George as Devon, a teenager who tries to seduce a modest and mild-mannered businessman (played by Joshua Townshend-Zellner). The film makes use of clips from ''[[The Adventures of Ford Fairlane]]'', but as [[Andrew Dice Clay]] (who played Fairlane) had been banned from MTV, he is not shown in any of the clips. The video was a huge hit and was placed in heavy rotation on MTV. Idol and George recreated the opening of the video for the 1991 [[Grammy Award|Grammys]]. An alternative version of the video does not feature the movie's footage, instead depicting a man playing the guitar as heard in the track.

At the 1990 [[MTV]] [[MTV VMA|Video Music Awards]], the video was nominated for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Male Video|Best Male Video]] and [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Special Effects|Best Special Effects]] and won the award for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Video from a Film|Best Video from a Film]].<ref>[http://theenvelope.latimes.com/factsheets/awardsdb/env-awards-db-search,0,7169155.htmlstory?searchtype=all&query=billy+idol&x=11&y=8 "Past Winners Database"]. ''[[Los Angeles Times]]''. 1990. Retrieved 4 November 2007.</ref> The video was voted number 33 on [[VH1]]'s 50 Sexiest Video Moments.

{{Refimprove section|date=November 2021}}
thumb|A photo of Billy Idol taken during the Cradle of Love Tour. The jacket is the same jacket that he wears in the video.
The video, directed by David Fincher, features footage of Idol singing in large painting frames throughout an apartment. The director made the decision to film Idol from the waist up as he was unable to walk due to injuries from a February 1990 motorcycle crash. The video also features Betsy Lynn George as Devon, a teenager who tries to seduce a modest and mild-mannered businessman (played by Joshua Townshend-Zellner). The film makes use of clips from The Adventures of Ford Fairlane, but as Andrew Dice Clay (who played Fairlane) had been banned from MTV, he is not shown in any of the clips. The video was a huge hit and was placed in heavy rotation on MTV. Idol and George recreated the opening of the video for the 1991 Grammys. An alternative version of the video does not feature the movie's footage, instead depicting a man playing the guitar as heard in the track.

At the 1990 MTV Video Music Awards, the video was nominated for Best Male Video and Best Special Effects and won the award for Best Video from a Film. The video was voted number 33 on VH1's 50 Sexiest Video Moments.

sections.heading: Cover versions
sections.wikitext: [[Alvin and the Chipmunks]] covered this song as the opening track to their 1991 album ''[[The Chipmunks Rock the House]]''. In 1992, [["Weird Al" Yankovic]] included the chorus as the first song in his polka medley "[[Polka Your Eyes Out]]" from his album ''[[Off the Deep End]]''.
sections.text: Alvin and the Chipmunks covered this song as the opening track to their 1991 album The Chipmunks Rock the House. In 1992, "Weird Al" Yankovic included the chorus as the first song in his polka medley "Polka Your Eyes Out" from his album Off the Deep End.
